_about: Every sentence the voice lab draws (D-073, D-074). A number is never typed here: it is a {token} the generator fills (gen-voice-lab.mjs), or a {{token}} the page fills while it runs. The build stops on a typed number, a word D-018 took out, a he, him or his, and a {token} left unfilled. Words are short and plain: what a thing is and does.

page.h1: Which voice should read your summaries aloud?
page.lede: This page reads one text in many voices. You change a setting, listen, and decide. A button then copies your pick as one line to paste back to me. The text starts as the {nSections} spoken summaries of the review page. You can edit it.
page.source: The text was read from the review page when this page was built. Your browser's voices are listed live. The local voices were made on this machine with Piper.
page.mineNote: A dashed value is my pick. A filled value is yours: the voice, speed, pitch and pause between sentences you pasted back are the default now. When you change a dashed value, it turns filled. The line at the end says which is which.

text.title: The text
text.take: Every voice below reads this text. Edit it, paste your own, or keep the review's summaries.

browser.title: Your browser's voices
browser.take: These are the voices your browser offers. They differ on every device. A voice marked online sends the text away to be read.

local.title: Local voices (Piper)
local.take: These voices are free and run on this machine. The samples are already made, so they play anywhere and need no internet.

notyet.title: Not here yet
notyet.take: More routes exist, and neither is set up yet. Each card says what it needs.

pick.title: Your pick
pick.take: Press copy and paste the line back to me. A value marked my pick is not a ruling.

bar.title: The bar at the top
bar.n: moves the reading and the page
bar.take: A skip moves the reading and takes the page to that section's text.

text.cap: A section is a heading line with no full stop, then its text. A blank line starts a new section.
text.viewLab: The text as it will be read
text.failed: Copy was blocked here. Select the text and copy it.
text.none: There is no text yet. Type some in the box.
text.noSpeech: This browser cannot speak. Open the page in Chrome or Edge to read the text aloud. The rest of the page still works.

browser.cap: The list is read live from your browser. A voice marked on this device works offline. A voice marked online needs the internet and sends the text to its maker.
browser.loading: Waiting for your browser to list its voices...
browser.none: Your browser offers no voices here. Open this page in Chrome or Edge on your own computer to hear them.
browser.noneEn: No English voice here. Press All languages to see the rest.
browser.tipLocal: Works offline. Nothing leaves your computer.
browser.tipOnline: Needs the internet. The text is sent to the voice's maker.
browser.sampleLine: This is how I would read your summary, one short sentence after another.

settings.head: Settings
settings.note: Each change applies from the next sentence. The text is read sentence by sentence, so a pause or a skip lands exactly.

rate.label: Speed
rate.what: How fast the voice talks. {rateNormal} is normal.

pitch.label: Pitch
pitch.what: How high the voice sounds. {pitchNormal} is normal.

pauseSection.label: Pause between sections
pauseSection.what: The silence before the next section starts.

readTitles.label: Read the section names
readTitles.what: Say each section's name before its text.

settings.yoursTip: Press to go back to the default.
settings.voiceMissing: Your voice, {{name}}, is not offered by this browser, so {{used}} reads for it. Open the page in Chrome to hear yours. Your pick stays as it is.
settings.enginePiper: Your pick is a Piper voice, so it cannot be read live here. The live reading uses the browser voice shown.

compare.head: Compare voices
compare.cap: Tick the voices you want to compare on the cards above, choose a sentence, and press compare. Each voice reads that one sentence, one after another, with the settings above.
compare.none: Tick at least one voice first.

local.cap: Piper makes speech on this computer, and nothing is sent anywhere. Each voice below reads the first summary, called {sampleTitle}, at {nSpeeds} speeds. Press play, then pick the one you like.
local.speedHelp: A speed is Piper's own setting. It stretches or squeezes the sounds without changing the voice.

notyet.failed: Copy was blocked here. Select the command and copy it.

cards.name: ElevenLabs
cards.what: The most natural voices of all. It runs on their servers, so the text leaves this machine. The free plan gives {elCredits} credits a month.
cards.need: It needs your API key from your ElevenLabs account. Give it to me when you want to try it. I would then run the command with your key in place.

cards.name: Kokoro
cards.what: The best free voice that runs on this machine. It makes the speech here, so nothing is sent away.
cards.need: It fails here until one system package is installed. That package turns words into sounds. You run the command once in your terminal, and it asks for your password.

pick.cap: This line carries your choice. It opens on the pick you pasted back, and it changes as you change a setting. Your pick is also kept in this browser, and the review page reads it.

pick.copied: Copied. Paste it back to me.
pick.failed: Copy was blocked here. Select the line and copy it.
pick.notYet: Nothing is kept until you change a value.
pick.notSaved: This browser would not keep it. Copy the line.

bar.cap: While a voice reads, a bar sticks to the top of the page. It has play and pause, stop, the previous and next section, every section as a chip with the one being read lit, and the speed. A skip moves the reading and takes the page to that section's text, which is highlighted while it is read.
bar.modeNote: While a voice reads is the default. Always is my addition, drawn dashed.
